_note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Rainbow Children's Medicare (consolidated, ₹ crore). One reportable segment, so the engine runs on a single revenue-growth path and a post-Ind AS 116 EBITDA margin (Screener basis: rent is not in EBITDA; lease interest sits in interest and right-of-use depreciation in depreciation; lease liabilities sit in borrowings, so the model's net cash is net of leases). The bed build (mature hospitals, new hospitals, pipeline) sits in `businessLines`; the authoring script checks that it sums to model revenue. Profit is attributable to owners (RAINBOW.patch.js); the tax line carries the 24% minorities in the acquired hospitals. Valued on EV/EBITDA, as the street does.
_revenueWhy: From the bed build below (beds × 365 × occupancy × ARPOB, plus pipeline hospitals). FY27 +22%: Q1 +33% (organic ~24%; acquisitions ₹38 cr), Q2 guided 'above 20%', the acquisition boost fades from Q3 (Guwahati and Warangal were consolidated from Aug-25 and Jul-25) and the 2026 monsoon was late and deficient; management guides ~20% and 'cross ₹2,000 cr'. FY28 +21%, FY29 +20%: ARPOB +5-6% a year (management: ARPP 5-6%), occupancy of new hospitals rising from 34% toward the mid-40s, and the pipeline (Malad, Coimbatore, Gurugram, Pune) starting with low occupancy. Management's medium-term ambition is ~20% a year (double revenue in four years after FY27).

businessLines._why: Mature = the 1,202 operational beds that management classifies as mature from FY27 (Q1FY27: occupancy 45.0%, ARPOB ₹70,662). Full-year occupancy has run ~6-8pp above Q1 (FY25 50.5% vs 42.4%; FY26 46.3% vs 40.2%) and ARPOB ~2-5% below Q1, so FY27 mature = 50.5% and ₹67,500 (a normal-to-weak season after a late monsoon), then +1-1.5pp of occupancy and +5-6% ARPOB a year (still below the 56% mature occupancy of FY25). New = the 10 hospitals under five years old (Q1FY27: 660 operational of 885 capacity beds, occupancy 34.4%, ARPOB ₹59,133): operational beds rise as HRBR, Electronic City and Warangal fill (690 / 760 / 800 weighted), occupancy 38% / 43% / 46%, ARPOB ₹57,000 / 60,400 / 63,500. Pipeline revenue is GAM's estimate per hospital (beds × months open × ~25-45% occupancy × ₹45,000-85,000 ARPOB, by city), using the opening dates management gave on 31-Jul-2026; we assume slow ramps for the Gurugram hub and Pune.

_marginWhy: Post-Ind AS EBITDA margin (Screener basis): 33% FY24-25, 32.2% FY26, 28.7% in Q1FY27 (29.5% a year earlier). Management guides the pre-Ind AS margin back to 24-25% for FY27 (Q1FY27 23.0%; FY26 26.3%); rent is ~5pp of revenue (Ind AS impact ₹96 cr in FY26, ₹26 cr in Q1FY27), so 24.5-25% pre-Ind AS ≈ 29.7-30.2% post. FY28 30.5%: HRBR and Electronic City break even (12-18 months guided), offset by start-up losses at Malad, Coimbatore and Gurugram Sector 56. FY29 30.0%: the 325-bed Gurugram hub, Pune and Seegehalli open. Each 1pp of margin is ~₹25 cr of FY28E EBITDA (~5% of EPS).
_capexWhy: Cash capex ₹380 / 460 / 480 cr plus new leases (right-of-use additions) ₹100 / 120 / 100 cr. Cash: maintenance ~₹45 cr a year; Gurugram ₹400-500 cr over two years (own land, own build); other projects at ₹65-70 lakh a bed (Coimbatore 130, Pune 150, Indore 100, Seegehalli 80, Malad fit-out); five-year plan ₹2,200 cr for 2,500 beds (~₹440 cr a year). FY26 capex ₹217 cr, Q1FY27 ₹56 cr. New leases are added because the model's net debt includes lease liabilities: right-of-use additions were ₹146 cr in FY26 (AR note 2.32), and Guntur, Malad, Indore and Seegehalli are leased. Engine workaround: a new lease adds an asset and a liability without cash, which the engine can only show as capex funded from net cash. The Nellore acquisition price is not disclosed and is left out.
_depWhy: FY26 depreciation ₹151 cr (incl. right-of-use depreciation ₹54 cr) = 6.6% of average gross block (₹2,294 cr); Q1FY27 ₹42 cr (₹169 cr annualised). 6.5% gives FY27E ≈ ₹181 cr with the new hospitals; the engine depreciates capex at once while projects sit in CWIP.
_treasuryWhy: Set to zero because the engine applies the yield to net cash after lease liabilities, which is negative (₹583 cr of cash, deposits and investments less ₹891 cr of leases at Mar-26). Treasury income is built on gross cash in `otherIncome` instead.
_otherIncomeWhy: Built from sourced parts (AR FY26 note 2.21). (1) Treasury income = yield × opening gross cash, deposits and mutual funds: FY26 ₹38.4 cr (bank interest ₹8.0 cr + mutual-fund gains ₹30.4 cr) on ~₹645 cr average funds = ~6.0%; company cash & investments ₹594 cr (Mar-26) and ₹613 cr (Jun-26). We take 6.25% on ₹594 / 600 / 610 cr opening funds (capex roughly absorbs free cash flow): ₹37 / 37.5 / 38 cr. (2) Recurring non-treasury interest (loans ₹1.7 cr and other financial assets ₹1.9 cr, unchanged FY25-26): ₹3.6 cr, held at ₹4-5 cr. One-offs left out: asset-sale gain ₹1.2 cr, write-backs ₹0.5 cr, FX. FY27E ₹41 cr vs FY26 ₹43.8 cr and the twelve months to Jun-26 ₹36.5 cr (Screener).

otherTreasury._why: Bank deposits reported under other financial assets, not in Screener's cash or investments: ₹104 cr non-current + ₹49 cr current at Mar-26 (AR notes 2.3a/b) less ₹7.8 cr earmarked for CSR and bank guarantees. With Screener's cash (₹34 cr) and mutual funds (₹404 cr) this gives the company's ₹583-594 cr.

_interestWhy: All finance cost is lease interest: ₹77.6 cr in FY26 on ₹764-891 cr of lease liabilities (~9%); ₹21.2 cr in Q1FY27 (₹85 cr annualised). New leases (~₹100-120 cr a year) add ~₹9-10 cr a year.
_taxWhy: Tax plus minorities (engine workaround: there is no minority line). Q1FY27: PBT ₹84.0 cr, tax ₹21.4 cr (25.5%), attributable PAT ₹60.6 cr = 27.8% leakage (minorities ~2.3%). FY26 effective tax 21.4% included a one-off ₹13 cr deferred-tax credit at Rosewalk; underlying ~25.5%. Minorities: 24% of Prashanthi and Pratiksha (₹3 cr in FY26, ₹2 cr in Q1FY27); the Malad JV with doctors adds more from FY28.
_payoutWhy: Dividend ~13-14% of profit since listing (₹3 a share paid in FY26, ₹30 cr); capex absorbs the rest.

dcf._betaWhy: No borrowings; lease liabilities are ~6% of enterprise value, so WACC (~11.0-11.1%) is close to the 11.3% cost of equity the engine uses. Defensive demand, but expansion risk outside the home markets.
dcf._tgWhy: Births are flat in India, but paediatric and maternity care is moving to organised, specialised hospitals and prices rise 5-6% a year: 6% nominal, the top of the house range.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~20% to 9% by year 15: bed additions slow and the network matures.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 31% post-Ind AS (~26% pre-Ind AS): back near FY26 once the 2026-29 openings mature, but below FY24-25 (33%) as more beds sit in costlier markets (NCR, Mumbai).
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex incl. new leases falls from ~19-23% of revenue (expansion) to 11%: replacement of the asset base (depreciation ~8.5% of revenue) plus growth capex for 6-9% growth.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: A normal paediatric season returns, new hospitals reach 45%+ occupancy a year early, Mumbai and Gurugram open on time with high-acuity mix, and the margin recovers toward 32% (pre-Ind AS ~26.5%).

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Two more weak seasons, occupancy stuck near 41-45%, the expansion outside the South (NCR, Mumbai, Pune, Indore) ramps slowly and burns cash, and the margin falls toward 28% (pre-Ind AS ~23%).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: How the street values Rainbow: EV/EBITDA on FY28E (Prabhudas Lilladher 28x pre-Ind AS EBITDA, ICICI Securities 25x, Anand Rathi 22x). We use post-Ind AS EBITDA with lease liabilities in net debt (the model basis; consistent because rent is excluded from EBITDA and the lease debt is counted). 20x = Rainbow's 21.5x median one-year-forward EV/EBITDA since listing (May-2022; no trough years: forward EBITDA never fell below half its prior peak), cut by the 7.4% median de-rating of six listed hospital peers versus their five-year median EV/EBITDA on 30-Sep-2026 (Apollo, Max, Fortis, Narayana, Medanta, Jupiter; KIMS and Aster left out because new-hospital losses and the 2024 GCC demerger distort their history) = 19.9x, rounded to 20x. No growth adjustment: our faster EBITDA growth (~18% a year FY26-29E vs 11% FY23-26) is bought with capex into new markets at lower returns. Bull 24.5x and bear 18x = the 75th and 25th percentiles of its forward EV/EBITDA since listing.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: Cross-check on earnings. 39x = Rainbow's 44.9x median one-year-forward P/E since listing (forwardMedian; no trough years) cut by the 13.5% median P/E de-rating of the same six hospital peers versus their five-year medians on 30-Sep-2026 (38.8x). Bull 47x, bear 32x scale with the EV/EBITDA multiples.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF (capex includes new leases), Ke 11.3%, terminal growth 6%, less net lease liabilities.
